target_customer: Retail investors in the UAE and wider GCC wanting commission-free access to US and local stocks, with Sharia screening
problem: Residents of the Gulf had costly or limited access to global markets and Sharia compliant investing.
business_model: Brokerage app with commission-free trading, revenue from fees on services, FX and premium features

founders.name: Feras Jalbout
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: former asset manager and VC turned builder and angel investor. Employers and education not listed.

founders.name: Kunal Taneja
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: executive business and technology leader with over two decades of experience in digital transformation, product management and cybersecurity.

competitors.name: Robinhood
competitors.what: US commission-free trading app used as the global comparison

technical_complexity.rationale: Brokerage app with custody and market data integrations is standard fintech engineering; the harder part is regulation.

defensibility.rationale: DFSA licence in DIFC (approved 2021) and localisation (Arabic, Sharia screener) are barriers, though the product is similar to others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Press cites Robinhood, eToro, Interactive Brokers and Sarwa as comparison points; no source shows any of them copying or buying Baraka.

market_need_then: Retail investor boom in commission-free apps; coverage in 2021 says the Gulf lacked commission-free access in local currency and Arabic. Regulatory approval from the DFSA in July 2021.

branding.brand_signature: Arabic word for blessing with Sharia investing features
branding.community_and_virality: Founder interviews and regional press (The National, Entrepreneur Middle East, YourStory); no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Meaningful Arabic name fits a Sharia friendly regional brand and gained regional press, but no source says the name drove growth; the name origin is not stated by the founder.

outcome_analysis: Baraka received DFSA approval in July 2021, launched across several GCC markets, raised a 4 million dollar seed in August 2021 and a 20 million dollar Series A led by Valar Ventures in November 2022, totalling about 25 million dollars. It now offers US and GCC stocks, options and gold with Sharia filters. It remains independent; no later round found.
notes: Pre-seed $1M described as earlier in 2021 in one search summary of coverage; exact date and investors unverified, recorded with year only. Competitor entries come from a National article whose exact date was not confirmed, so source_date is null. Series A stated by The National and Zawya (company press release). Series A existing investors included Class 5 Global, Global Founders Capital and VentureSouq. No Series B found. Founder education and employers not found. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
